title: WPSS/1092/2020 of BUDDHI BALLABH BHATT Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
WPSS No. 1092 of 2020
Hon 'b le Man oj Ku m ar Tiw ar i, J.

Mr. B.S. Koranga, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. Rakesh Kunwar, Additional
C.S.C. for the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. N.S. Pundir, Advocate for
respondent nos. 2 to 5.
Heard learned counsel for the
parties.
Petitioner earlier filed WPSS No.
2688 of 2019, seeking correction of his
date of birth as recorded in his service
book, which was disposed of by a
Co-ordinate Bench of this Court on
10.12.2019, directing the Com petent
Authority to take decision on petitioner's
representation. Now, Com petent
Authority has taken a decision on
25.02.2020, whereby petitioner's request
for correction of his date of birth in
service book has been rejected. I n this
writ petition, petitioner has challenged
the said order.
The reason assigned in the rejection
order is that, at the tim e of petitioner's
appointment, his date of birth was
recorded as 02.05.1964, based on
inform ation furnished by him and he had
also put his signature in the relevant
page of service book.
Learned counsel for respondent
nos. 2 to 5 has placed reliance upon
provision contained in sub-Rule 3 of Rule
8-B of U.P. State Electricity Board
Operation Employees Class Service
Rules, 1995, which provides that date of

birth, as recorded in the service book,
cannot be changed.
Learned counsel for petitioner has
placed reliance upon High School
Certificate issued in favour of petitioner,
in which his date of birth is mentioned as
02.05.1966.
Learned counsel for respondent
nos. 2 to 5 subm its that petitioner was
appointed on the post of Line Coolie on
18.06.1984 and he passed High School
Examination in 1990, therefore his High
School Certificate, which was issued
after his regular appointment, cannot be
looked at for changing his date of birth
as recorded in the service book. He also
produced in Court service book of the
petitioner, in original, wherein date of
birth of the petitioner is indicated as
02.05.1964 and petitioner has also
signed on the page where his date of
birth is mentioned.
This Court finds substance in the
contention raised by learned counsel for
respondent nos. 2 to 5 that date of birth
as m entioned in High School certificate
issued to petitioner after his appointm ent
cannot be relied for correction of his date
of birth.
I t is settled position in law that
request for correction of date of birth
cannot be entertained at the fag end of
service career of an em ployee.
I n such view of the m atter, this
Court is not inclined to interfere in the
m atter.
Accordingly, the writ petition fails
and is dismissed.

( Man oj Ku m ar Tiw ar i, J.)
 30.09.2022
Arpan
